image_prompt.text: Scattered wooden crates and low broken walls across the open ground, spaced so players can duck behind them and break the zombies' line of sight
A central abandoned building as the focal structure of the map, boarded up and derelict, its footprint dominating the middle of the enclosed ground
A perimeter fence enclosing the whole map, chain-link and patched, marking the edge of the survivable area
A spooky, dark atmosphere over the whole site — overcast night, deep shadow between the crates and the building, decayed and abandoned

layout_placement.text: Zombie entry points around the fence line, with the open ground between the perimeter and the central building as the horde's approach and patrol area

notes: Preset caveat: took Horde Defense on its own shape (arena-contained) but dropped `destructible-cluster` — the prompt asks for a static abandoned building and never mentions structures collapsing, and welded collapsing geometry would be an unrequested instruction to the image model.
The perimeter fence is what the `arena-contained` BoundaryZone is made of here; it is also carried as free text in `image_prompt` so its geometry survives into the image stream.

The abandoned building is emitted as exterior geometry only. Nothing in the prompt says players go inside, so `building-interior` (P3) was not taken; if the shelter should be enterable this becomes P3, which is not ready yet.

The request to expose 'BuildingSize', 'CrateCount' and 'FenceHeight' as adjustable attributes is not map geometry and has no option or list entry — it is a parameterisation of the generated instances (the central building, the crate cover cluster, the perimeter fence) for whatever consumes this handoff.
No count fields: the prompt states no quantities. 'Small' is a scale band, and 'scattered crates' gives no number.

would have asked: Sounds like a horde-defense layout — one fenced-in arena you hold out in, a central abandoned building as the anchor, crates scattered for cover to break zombie sightlines, and zombie spawn points set around the fence line, all under a dark spooky night. That builds on the proven pipeline. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: Should the central abandoned building be enterable — somewhere to actually run inside and hide — or is it a sealed derelict shell you take cover around? Going indoors needs interiors generated separately, which is a slower build and is not available yet, so I built it as an exterior landmark.
would have asked: Do you want the buildings breaking apart as the horde pushes through, or should everything stay standing? I left the collapsing-structure part of the preset out.
